h: A Gentle North Lincolnshire Day Out
p: Messingham is a pleasant village south of Scunthorpe, and the zoo fits neatly into a quiet country day. Because it's a manageable size, you can let children set the pace, go back for a second look at their favourite animals and not worry about missing anything. Talking to the keepers is one of the best bits of visiting a smaller zoo, as they know every animal by name and personality, so encourage the kids to ask questions.

If you're local, the zoo makes a great go-to for half-term or an easy Saturday. If you're coming from further afield, it sits within easy reach of the M180 and the M18, so getting here from Doncaster, Hull, Grimsby or Lincoln is simple. Wear something warm, as the open countryside can be blowy, and bring a snack bag for the little ones.

There's more nature on the doorstep. Messingham Sand Quarry, a Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve near the village, has lakes, reedbeds and heath created from old sand workings, and it's lovely for a short walk and some birdwatching. Back in Scunthorpe, the North Lincolnshire Museum tells the story of the area from prehistoric times to the steel industry, which is a nice change of pace on a wet day. Further south, Gainsborough Old Hall is one of the best-preserved medieval manor houses in England, while Brigg's market town streets are pleasant for a mooch and a brew. Put it all together and it's a satisfying day without a long drive.
